title: Decoupled Toolflow SDK Microprotocol — PRD draft
body:
Context:
This doc sketches a lightweight, intentionally decoupled microprotocol and SDK ergonomics for the Hosted API that focuses on three concurrent product priorities: low-latency streaming, safe/tool-aware invocation, and compact structured output for constrained clients (mobile, embedded). The goal is a minimal runtime contract that: (a) enables progressive results, (b) allows safe handoff and validation of tool calls, and (c) makes client SDKs small and easy to reason about (no heavy dependency on the full streaming stack).

Why a new microprotocol?
- Existing streaming flows in Hosted API are powerful but carry a lot of coupling between: session semantics, tool orchestration, and rich typed outputs. That coupling increases SDK complexity and leads to brittle client integrations.
- Many teams (mobile, edge) want a predictable tiny surface: incremental frames + explicit commit/abort for tool calls + compact schema hints instead of full typed payloads.
- We want to experiment with a protocol that favors graceful degradation: clients fall back to a single final JSON output if streaming fails.

High-level product goals
- User-visible: faster perceived time-to-first-token and earlier tool suggestions in UIs that assemble outputs progressively.
- Developer-visible: SDKs that are <200KB minified for commonly used languages and expose 3-4 primitives (connect, onFrame, callTool, finalize).
- Safety/ops: explicit, auditable tool-call lifecycle with telemetry hooks and runtime-level indirection for fallback (model -> tool shadowing).

Non-goals
- This PRD does not propose a replacement for the full typed-tool handshake currently used for advanced server-side orchestrations.
- It does not address Dedicated/Private deployment differences in depth (assume control plane parity initially).

Personas
- Product engineer: wants to embed quick suggestions (e.g., code completions, content snippets) into their app with predictable latency and a tiny client lib.
- Platform engineer: wants observability hooks for token-level timings and tool-call audit trails.
- Solutions engineer: will use the protocol to validate integration complexity during POC with enterprise customers.

User flows (happy path)
1) Client opens a streaming session (HTTP/2 or WebSocket). Client sends an initial manifest: small JSON with model, max_tokens, fallback_profile.
2) Server starts sending compact frames: each frame is newline-delimited, begins with a 1-byte type marker (T=token, M=meta, O=output-hint, C=call), followed by a base64-encoded payload when non-ASCII.
3) When the model signals a tool invocation, server emits a C frame: {call_id, tool_id, brief_schema_hint, confidence}. Client SDK exposes onToolProposed(call) and returns either: accept, defer, or decline.
4) If accepted, an explicit commit flow: client invokes callTool(call_id, args) that the server routes to toolchain. Tool progress is streamed back as T/M/O frames and a final call-complete frame.
5) Finalization: server emits a commit frame linking the produced structured artifact and the final natural language explanation. If streaming disrupted, server emits a final-condensed JSON for the client to hydrate state.

Protocol primitives (concise)
- Connect(manifest) -> session_id
- onFrame(frame) -> token/meta/call/events
- callTool(call_id, payload) -> ack
- finalize(session_id) -> final_object OR condensed_final_json

Frame design decisions (compactness + extensibility)
- Single-byte frame type to keep start-up parsing cheap for tiny runtimes.
- Prefer inline short schema hints (tiny vocabulary) over full schemas — helps low-bandwidth clients present consistent UI affordances without heavy parsing.
- Binary payloads are base64 to keep HTTP friendly; future plan: optional CBOR/MessagePack channels negotiated in manifest.

Structured output model
- Instead of heavy typed JSON payloads, we surface 3 layers: hint, proto, and committed artifact.
  - hint: tiny suggestion of the structure (e.g., [action:search, fields:query,snippets])
  - proto: a shallow key-value map with small typed tokens (string/id/enum)
  - committed artifact: canonical full JSON blob stored in server-side artifact store and referenced by ID (artifact_id) in the final commit frame
- Motivation: keep wire costs low, avoid double-parsing on clients, and let the server manage heavyweight storage.

SDK ergonomics (language-agnostic principles)
- Minimal API surface: connect, subscribe, acceptTool, sendToolArgs, close.
- Event-first model: callbacks/promises for frames; encourage apps to incrementally render tokens and UI widgets from hints.
- Backpressure: SDK maintains a tiny leaky-bucket and exposes simple isReady() to avoid UI freezes. Default client behavior: buffer up to N frames (configurable) then trigger onBackpressure event to application.
- Pluggable validation: small validator hooks allow apps to run lightweight client-side sanity checks on proto frames (length, allowed enums) before accepting tool calls. Core lib ships with no heavy validator, customers can opt in.

Safety & tool calling semantics
- Every tool proposal must include: call_id, tool_id, minimal security label (user-initiated|system-initiated), and a human_readable_hint.
- Default: client must explicitly accept tool proposals (no auto-commits) unless the manifest sets tool_auto_accept:true and the client is authorized.
- Audit trail: each call commit emits a trace: [session_id, call_id, timestamp, actor, tool_snapshot_id]. These are surfaced to Console for post-hoc review and can be filtered by policy.

Observability & instrumentation
- Minimal metrics to emit: ttf-token, ttf-tool-proposal, tool-latency, session-duration, frame-drop-rate.
- Traces: prefer lightweight spans tied to session_id and call_id. SDKs should attach optional client tags (app_version, platform).

Fallback & graceful degradation
- If streaming is interrupted or client declines a tool, server falls back to: final_condensed_json which contains the final artifact_id and a textual fallback that is resilient to client parsing errors.
- Clients should be resilient: if they miss a commit frame, they do a short poll GET /session/{id}/final.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (canary): internal web + mobile apps (3 teams) adopt microprotocol behind a feature flag (1 month). Validate SDK size, token-first-latency improvement, and tool-selection UX.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable opt-in for public customers with small traffic caps and telemetry enabled (2 months).
- Phase 2 (general availability): full Console integration for artifact browsing, SLA guarding of tool calls, and docs.

Success metrics
- Primary: median time to first token improved by >= 15% for supported clients.
- Secondary: average SDK payload size <200KB (gzip) for JS/Android/iOS builds.
- Safety metric: percentage of tool proposals explicitly accepted by clients (target <= 20% auto-accept in opt-in customers).

Open questions / risks
- How do existing typed-tool integrations map onto hint/proto/commit flow? (TODO: migration guide draft)
- Is base64-on-HTTP the right long-term wire choice for mobile networks? Evaluate CBOR vs base64 in Phase 0 labs.
- Operational complexity: artifact store increases storage/retention needs and affects privacy audit surfaces. Need legal and security review (contact: Yvonne Chen).

Immediate next steps
- Engineering spike: implement minimal server-side emitter for C frames + commit artifact store preview (RED-4132).
- SDK spike: JS + Kotlin minimal runtime with event-first callback (PR: github PR linked above).
- UX: design micro-interaction patterns for tool proposal affordances in mobile UI (owner: Tomás).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: focus on delivering a small, testable contract that teams can adopt quickly. Expect follow-ups around migration, telemetry, and privacy.
- Please add comments inline where wording is ambiguous or implementation constraints are missing.
